nodes.text: Let $\alpha>0$ and $n\geq 1$. Let $F(n,\alpha)$ be the largest $k$ such that there exists some 2-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ in which any induced subgraph $H$ on at least $k$ vertices contains more than $\alpha\binom{\lvert H\rvert}{2}$ many edges of each colour. Prove that for every fixed $0\leq \alpha \leq 1/2$, as $n\to\infty$,\[F(n,\alpha)\sim c_\alpha \log n\]for some constant $c_\alpha$.

#162 : [Er90b,p.21] combinatorics | ramsey theory | discrepancy It is easy to show with the probabilistic method that there exist $c_1(\alpha),c_2(\alpha)$ such that\[c_1(\alpha)\log n < F(n,\alpha) < c_2(\alpha)\log n.\] Additional thanks to : Wouter Cames van Batenberg and KoishiChan Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
